wrong_answers.text: Fly at a lower altitude to avoid clouds.

question: What are important considerations when parking an airplane outside a designated, supervised area?

correct_answers.text: Select a location and heading that prevents propeller or jet blast from striking the airplane unnecessarily.
Park the airplane headed into the existing or forecast wind whenever possible.
Allow the airplane to roll straight ahead enough to straighten the nosewheel or tailwheel after stopping.

wrong_answers.text: Park the airplane with the tail facing the wind.
Always park the airplane in the shade to avoid overheating.
Select a parking location based solely on convenience.
Ignore the direction of the wind when parking.
Ensure the airplane is parked on a slope for drainage.
Park as close as possible to other airplanes for efficiency.
Always park with the nosewheel or tailwheel turned.
Select a parking spot based on proximity to the terminal.

source: Airplane Flying Handbook (FAA-H-8083-3C) Chapter 2: Ground Operations Introduction, Section: Parking

question: What are important steps to take when securing an airplane after a flight?

correct_answers.text: Inspect for oil or fuel streaks around the cowling.
Check and adjust oil levels to AFM/POH levels.
Fill fuel tanks to prevent water condensation if inactive.

wrong_answers.text: Leave fuel tanks empty to reduce weight.
Tighten chains completely to prevent movement.
Ignore tire condition if they appear inflated.
Skip inspection if the airplane looks fine.
Use only chains for tie downs regardless of conditions.
Hangar the airplane without checking space allocation.
Rely solely on visual inspection without touching components.

source: Airplane Flying Handbook (FAA-H-8083-3C) Chapter 2: Ground Operations Introduction, Securing and Servicing

Failing to evaluate ability to act as PIC
